title: Amazon Locker
prompt: Design a locker system for Amazon package pickup. A customer orders a package and chooses locker delivery at checkout. The system must assign the package to an available compartment (small/medium/large) based on package dimensions. When delivery arrives, an agent scans the barcode and places the package in the assigned slot. The customer receives an OTP and retrieves the package by entering the code at the locker. Packages expire after 3 days if not picked up.

stages.title: Requirements
stages.questionPrompt: Clarify the requirements. What's in scope and what isn't?
stages.howToAnswer: Capture the rules tightly. Decide whether to scope: multi-locker networks, persistent storage, customer notifications. State assumptions out loud.

exampleHints.headline: Example (Movie Theater Booking):
bullets: Assign available seats by size / section
Out of Scope: pricing, refunds, network scale

must: Package has dimensions (length, width, height) and must fit in a slot
Locker has multiple compartments with size classes (small/medium/large)
Assign package to best-fit compartment (avoid oversizing)
OTP generation and validation for pickup
Package expiration after 3 days
should: Delivery agent assignment to locker by zip code
Locker availability (open/closed/maintenance)
Notification on assignment / pickup ready
avoid: Designing customer notification system in detail
Building a UI or network protocol

stages.sampleAnswer:
Scope:
- Package dimensions, slot sizes, best-fit assignment
- OTP-based pickup validation
- Package state machine: assigned → stored → picked-up OR expired
- Single locker or static set of lockers at a location
- Delivery agent delivery to locker

Out of scope:
- Multi-locker network load-balancing
- Persistent database schema
- Email/SMS notifications
- Real-time tracking across the supply chain
hints: What does a package look like? What properties matter for fitting into a slot?
How do you find an available compartment that fits the package without wasting space?
What events happen to a package from assignment to pickup or expiry? Draw the state machine.

stages.title: Entities & Relationships
stages.questionPrompt: What are the core entities and how do they relate?
stages.howToAnswer: Pick the orchestrator. Decide what owns each piece of state: locker inventory, package state, OTP. Avoid mixing responsibilities.

exampleHints.headline: Example (Movie Theater):
bullets: Theater has Screens; Screen has Seats
Booking owns the assignment of customer to seat

must: AmazonLocker (orchestrator): owns slots, packages, OTP state
Slot: compartment with fixed size and availability flag
Package: tracks parcel with dimensions, state, assigned slot
PackageState enum: ASSIGNED, STORED, PICKED_UP, EXPIRED
OTP: security code tied to slot and expiry time
should: Size enum: SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE or dimension-based
DeliveryAgent: for agent-to-locker dispatch
Timestamp tracking: assignment, storage, pickup, expiry
avoid: God class that mixes slot management, package tracking, and OTP
Storing package dimensions inside slots — dimensions belong on Package

stages.sampleAnswer:
- AmazonLocker (orchestrator): orchestrates assignment, storage, and pickup. Owns collection of Slots and pending Packages. Generates OTPs.
- Slot: has size (SMALL/MEDIUM/LARGE), available (bool), assignedPackageId (optional).
- Package: has id, dimensions (length, width, height), state (enum), assignedSlot (reference), expiryTime (timestamp).
- OTP: has code (string), slotId, expiryTime.
- DeliveryAgent: has id, assignedZipCode, available (bool).
- Size enum: SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE with corresponding dimension ranges.
- PackageState enum: ASSIGNED (awaiting delivery), STORED (in locker), PICKED_UP (removed), EXPIRED (not picked in 3 days).
hints: What's the main entry point? Who drives the workflow (locker machine, system service, or agent)?
Where does the assignment logic live? On the Locker, on a separate strategy, or on Package?
What state must survive between operations? Package state, slot occupancy, OTP validity — who owns each?

stages.title: Class Design
stages.questionPrompt: Define the classes — fields and methods. Keep rules with the entity that owns the state.
stages.howToAnswer: Sketch each class with explicit method signatures and what they return / throw. Use enums for size, state, and status.

must: AmazonLocker.assignPackage(pkg) -> (Slot, OTP) or throws
AmazonLocker.storePackage(barcode, slotId) -> bool / Result
AmazonLocker.pickupPackage(slotId, otp) -> Package or throws InvalidOTP
Slot: size, available, assignedPackageId
Size enum (SMALL/MEDIUM/LARGE) or Dimension class
should: Best-fit slot selection: prefer smallest slot that fits
Package state transitions (enum: ASSIGNED, STORED, PICKED_UP, EXPIRED)
OTP generation and expiry validation
Configurable locker dimensions and size ranges via constructor
avoid: Returning bool from assignPackage — return the slot and OTP
Hard-coded size thresholds in multiple places

stages.sampleAnswer:
```
enum Size { SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE }
enum PackageState { ASSIGNED, STORED, PICKED_UP, EXPIRED }

class Dimension:
  length: int
  width: int
  height: int
  fitsInSize(size: Size) -> bool:
    (length, width, height) <= size's bounds

class Slot:
  slotId: str
  size: Size
  available: bool
  assignedPackageId: str?

class Package:
  packageId: str
  dimension: Dimension
  state: PackageState
  assignedSlotId: str?
  createdTime: timestamp
  expiryTime: timestamp (now + 3 days)

class OTP:
  code: str (6-digit random)
  slotId: str
  expiryTime: timestamp (now + 1 hour)
  isValid(code: str, now: timestamp) -> bool

class AmazonLocker:
  slots: Map<slotId, Slot>
  packages: Map<packageId, Package>
  otpMap: Map<slotId, OTP>
  sizeStrategy: SlotAssignmentStrategy
  
  assignPackage(pkg: Package) -> (slot: Slot, otp: OTP) throws NoAvailableSlot:
    matching = [s for s in slots if s.available and dimension.fitsInSize(s.size)]
    slot = sizeStrategy.selectSlot(matching)  // best-fit
    if not slot: throw NoAvailableSlot
    pkg.state = ASSIGNED
    pkg.assignedSlotId = slot.slotId
    pkg.expiryTime = now + 3 days
    slot.available = false
    slot.assignedPackageId = pkg.packageId
    otp = generateOTP(slot.slotId)
    return (slot, otp)
  
  storePackage(barcode: str, slotId: str) -> void:
    pkg = packages[barcode]
    if pkg.assignedSlotId != slotId: throw MismatchError
    pkg.state = STORED
    slot = slots[slotId]
    slot.assignedPackageId = pkg.packageId
  
  pickupPackage(slotId: str, otp: str) -> Package throws InvalidOTP:
    if not isValidOTP(slotId, otp): throw InvalidOTP
    slot = slots[slotId]
    pkg = packages[slot.assignedPackageId]
    pkg.state = PICKED_UP
    slot.available = true
    slot.assignedPackageId = null
    return pkg
  
  generateOTP(slotId: str) -> OTP:
    code = randomSixDigits()
    otp = OTP(code, slotId, now + 1 hour)
    otpMap[slotId] = otp
    return otp
  
  isValidOTP(slotId: str, code: str) -> bool:
    otp = otpMap[slotId]
    return otp and otp.code == code and otp.expiryTime > now
```
hints: Assignable package means mapping dimensions to size classes. Is Dimension a class or just three fields on Package?
Methods that mutate state should return rich results, not bare bool. assignPackage needs to return both the slot and the OTP.
State transitions are key — use an enum. When does a Package become EXPIRED? On a timer, or lazily on access?

stages.title: Implementation
stages.questionPrompt: Pseudo-code the assignment and pickup flows. Trace one end-to-end scenario.
stages.howToAnswer: The assignment (best-fit matching) and pickup (OTP validation + state transition) are the meaty parts. Trace a concrete sequence: package arrives → assigned to slot → stored → picked up.

must: assignPackage finds a fitting slot and returns it with OTP
Slot selection avoids oversizing (best-fit, not first-fit)
pickupPackage validates OTP and time before unlocking
Trace through one complete scenario end-to-end
should: Handle expiry: check and transition EXPIRED packages on access or via background job
Error cases: no available slot, invalid OTP, slot mismatch

stages.sampleAnswer:
```
assignPackage(pkg: Package) -> (Slot, OTP):
  // Find slots that fit the package dimension
  candidates = []
  for each slot in slots:
    if slot.available and pkg.dimension.fitsInSize(slot.size):
      candidates.append(slot)
  
  if candidates.empty(): throw NoAvailableSlot
  
  // Best-fit: prefer smallest slot that fits
  bestSlot = min(candidates, key=lambda s: s.size.volume())
  
  // Assign package to slot
  pkg.state = ASSIGNED
  pkg.assignedSlotId = bestSlot.slotId
  pkg.expiryTime = now + 3 days
  bestSlot.available = false
  bestSlot.assignedPackageId = pkg.packageId
  
  // Generate OTP
  otp = OTP(
    code = random6Digits(),
    slotId = bestSlot.slotId,
    expiryTime = now + 1 hour
  )
  otpMap[bestSlot.slotId] = otp
  
  return (bestSlot, otp)

pickupPackage(slotId: str, otpCode: str) -> Package:
  // Validate OTP
  otp = otpMap[slotId]
  if otp == null or otp.code != otpCode or otp.expiryTime < now:
    throw InvalidOTPException("OTP invalid or expired")
  
  // Unlock and release
  slot = slots[slotId]
  pkg = packages[slot.assignedPackageId]
  
  if pkg.state == EXPIRED:
    throw PackageExpiredException()
  
  pkg.state = PICKED_UP
  slot.available = true
  slot.assignedPackageId = null
  delete otpMap[slotId]
  
  return pkg

storePackage(barcode: str, slotId: str) -> void:
  pkg = packages[barcode]
  if pkg == null: throw PackageNotFound
  if pkg.assignedSlotId != slotId: throw SlotMismatchException
  
  pkg.state = STORED
  slot = slots[slotId]
  // Slot remains unavailable until pickup
```

Trace (end-to-end):
1. Package P1: 10×8×6 arrives. Locker has SMALL (12×10×8), MEDIUM (20×15×12), LARGE (30×20×15).
2. assignPackage(P1):
   - candidates = [SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE] (all fit)
   - bestSlot = SMALL (smallest that fits)
   - P1.state = ASSIGNED, P1.expiryTime = now + 3 days
   - SMALL.available = false, SMALL.assignedPackageId = P1
   - otp = OTP('123456', 'SMALL', now + 1 hour)
   - return (SMALL, otp) → Customer gets code '123456'
3. Delivery agent scans barcode P1, calls storePackage('P1', 'SMALL'):
   - P1.state = STORED
4. Customer arrives at locker, enters OTP '123456':
   - pickupPackage('SMALL', '123456'):
     - otp valid? yes
     - P1.state == EXPIRED? no
     - P1.state = PICKED_UP
     - SMALL.available = true
     - return P1
5. Locker dispenses P1.
hints: Pseudocode the candidate-finding loop first. Which fields make a slot a candidate?
Best-fit isn't just 'first available' — how do you minimize wasted space without over-engineering?
Trace one full scenario: arrival, assignment, storage, OTP validation, pickup. Does state flow correctly?

stages.title: Extensibility
stages.questionPrompt: How would you extend this for: different size strategies, multi-location networks, or priority packages?
stages.howToAnswer: Stay high-level. Point at the seams in the design that make the change clean.

must: Different slot-selection strategies: best-fit, first-fit, load-balanced
should: Multi-location: network of lockers with inter-locker transfers
Priority packages: skip the queue, prefer larger slots
avoid: Rewriting assignPackage logic for each strategy

stages.sampleAnswer:
Different slot strategies: SlotAssignmentStrategy interface with BestFitStrategy, FirstFitStrategy, LoadBalancedStrategy impls. AmazonLocker.sizeStrategy swaps at runtime — no change to assignPackage.

Multi-location network: introduce LockerNetwork service. Each Locker stays unchanged. Network.findLocker(pkg, location) searches nearby lockers, spilling to secondary locations. Network coordinates inter-locker transfers.

Priority packages: add priority field to Package. slotCandidates sorted by (size, then priority) — premium customers get medium slots even if large is available. No change to core Locker.
hints: What's the smallest abstraction that lets you swap slot-selection algorithms?
Multi-location: is each Locker independent, or does the Network own them? Who routes the package?
Priority: where does it affect the sort order? In assignPackage, or before entering the locker?

deepDives.title: Best-fit slot selection
deepDives.questionPrompt: Why is best-fit assignment better than first-fit? How would you implement it efficiently?
deepDives.sampleAnswer: First-fit assigns to the earliest available slot that fits, which leads to fragmentation — all SMALL slots fill up while LARGE remain empty, wasting space. Best-fit picks the smallest slot that fits the package, preserving larger slots for larger packages later. Efficiency: sort candidate slots by size, then pick the first. If slots are static (small number), O(n log n) upfront or O(log n) per query with a balanced tree. For a locker with 30 slots, O(30) per assignment is negligible.

must: Explain why first-fit causes fragmentation
Best-fit minimizes wasted compartment capacity
should: Discuss O(n log n) or O(log n) complexity depending on data structure
Note that static locker size makes optimization less critical
avoid: Claiming best-fit is always optimal (worst case is still NP for bin packing)

hints: Imagine you have SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE slots. A package fits in all three. Why does assigning to SMALL help future packages?
What data structure lets you find the minimum slot quickly? Sorted array? Priority queue?
Is the optimization worth the complexity for a locker with ~30 compartments?

deepDives.title: OTP security and expiry
deepDives.questionPrompt: How do you prevent OTP reuse, brute-force attacks, and ensure expiry without constant polling?
deepDives.sampleAnswer: OTP is single-use: after pickupPackage consumes an OTP, delete it from otpMap. Brute-force mitigation: rate-limit locker unlock attempts (e.g., max 3 attempts per minute) — wrong entry locks the slot briefly. Expiry: store expiryTime on OTP. Check on access (lazy). For large-scale: background job scans and invalidates expired OTPs hourly. OTP code itself: 6 digits gives 1M possibilities; for 1000 lockers with concurrent pickups, collision risk is low. If needed, use 8-digit codes or alphanumeric.

must: OTP is single-use (deleted after valid pickup)
Expiry checked on every pickup attempt
Rate-limiting on invalid attempts
should: Background job to clean expired OTPs
Configurable OTP length and validity window
avoid: Lazy cleanup leading to unbounded otpMap growth

hints: What happens if a customer enters the OTP twice? Once to open the locker, then again? Should it work the second time?
After 10 failed OTP attempts, should the locker lock down? Who resets it?
If otpMap grows unbounded, what's the worst-case memory impact?

deepDives.title: Package expiry handling
deepDives.questionPrompt: How do you handle packages that expire after 3 days? When and how do you clean them up?
deepDives.sampleAnswer: Mark packages EXPIRED lazily: on pickupPackage attempt, check expiryTime < now; if so, transition state to EXPIRED and throw PackageExpiredException. Separately, a background cleanup job runs daily: iterate all STORED packages, find those past expiryTime, mark EXPIRED, notify admin, and free the slot (set available=true). For a production system, EXPIRED packages stay in the database for audit/analytics (don't delete), but the slot is immediately reusable. OTP is also deleted (or marked invalid) when a package expires.

must: Check expiry on pickup attempt
Transition package to EXPIRED state
Free the slot for reuse
should: Background cleanup job to surface expired packages
Log/notify admin on expiry (refund, return logistics)
avoid: Blocking slots forever for expired packages

hints: When does a package transition from STORED to EXPIRED? On a timer, or when someone tries to pick it up?
If you check expiry lazily (on access), expired packages may sit in slots for days if no one tries to pick them up. How do you surface them?
Should an expired package's slot be available for new assignments? Or reserved for admin handling?
